subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/write/exec access boundary for that skill directory, or remain only a discovery, prompt, and command-visibility control?
rationale: The current wording and UI say a skill is disabled, but enforcing that as isolation would change public config semantics and touch security-sensitive tool and sandbox boundaries.

options.title: Make disabled skills inaccessible
options.body: Keep the existing UI/config wording and enforce denied skill roots for file tools and exec paths, with compatibility notes and targeted regression coverage.

options.title: Keep disable discovery-only
options.body: Document and rename the behavior as visibility-only, then point operators to sandbox, filesystem, and exec policies for real isolation.

options.title: Introduce a separate strict policy
options.body: Preserve current `enabled:false` compatibility and add an explicit strict skill-access policy for multi-user or untrusted-code deployments.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills inaccessible
recommendation.body: Keep the existing UI/config wording and enforce denied skill roots for file tools and exec paths, with compatibility notes and targeted regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses security posture, skill semantics, sandboxing, and public UX, and the history points to steipete as the strongest available routing owner for that boundary choice.
